- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (sentiment < 0.5) — model is overly conservative and misses upward momentum.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model lags sentiment shifts by 1–2 days, especially when sentiment rises sharply.
- Mean-reversion bias: model overcorrects after strong upward moves, leading to premature declines.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile or uncertain.
- When sentiment is high (>0.7) and price is rising, model often underestimates the continuation of the trend.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — model tends to follow recent price paths even when sentiment suggests reversal.
